document_title: Information Reporting and Transfer for Valuable Consideration Rules for Section 1035 Exchanges of Life Insurance and Certain Other Life Insurance Contract Transactions

claims.quote: Regardless of whether a contract is issued in a section 1035 exchange, it must be described in section 7702(a) to be considered a life insurance contract under the Code, which would require that it be treated as a life insurance contract under applicable State law.
claims.summary: A contract issued in a section 1035 exchange must be described in section 7702(a) to be considered a life insurance contract under the Code, requiring it to be treated as a life insurance contract under applicable State law.

claims.quote: Sec.  1.6050Y-3(a) of the 2023 proposed regulations would require reporting by each ``6050Y(b) issuer'' that is a ``section 1035 issuer'' with respect to each
claims.summary: The 2023 proposed regulations require reporting by each 6050Y(b) issuer that is a section 1035 issuer with respect to each reportable death benefit paid under contracts issued in section 1035 exchanges.

claims.quote: The 2023 proposed regulations would generally impose a reporting obligation on both the issuer of the old interest (old issuer) and the issuer of the new interest (new issuer) in a section 1035 exchange if the policyholder (seller) is exchanging an interest in a life insurance contract that has been transferred in an RPS.
claims.affected_party: issuer of the old interest, issuer of the new interest
claims.summary: Reporting obligation on both the old and new issuers in a section 1035 exchange if the policyholder is exchanging an interest in a life insurance contract transferred in an RPS.

claims.quote: The preamble to the 2023 proposed regulations indicated that it is anticipated that this reporting will be completed on Form 1099-SB, Seller's Investment in Life Insurance Contract, and the information to be provided would include the policy number and identification of the transaction as a section 1035 exchange.
claims.affected_party: issuer of the old interest, issuer of the new interest
claims.summary: Reporting on Form 1099-SB, including policy number and identification of the transaction as a section 1035 exchange.

claims.quote: The commenter suggested modifying Sec. 1.6050Y-3 of the 2019 final regulations to require the issuer of the existing RPS contract to furnish a statement to the issuer of a new contract received in exchange for the RPS contract in a section 1035 exchange.
claims.affected_party: issuer of the existing RPS contract
claims.summary: Issuer of the existing RPS contract must furnish a statement to the issuer of a new contract received in exchange for the RPS contract in a section 1035 exchange.

claims.quote: the filing of information returns with the IRS by the old issuer and new issuer with respect to section 1035 exchanges of RPS contracts is not necessary to accomplish the desired compliance goals.
claims.summary: The filing of information returns with the IRS by the old issuer and new issuer with respect to section 1035 exchanges of RPS contracts is not necessary.

claims.quote: the requirement under Sec.  1.6050Y-3(a) of the 2023 proposed regulations for section 1035 issuers (both old issuers described in Sec.  1.6050Y-1(a)(8)(v)(A) of the 2023 proposed regulations and new issuers described in Sec.  1.6050Y-1(a)(8)(v)(B) of the 2023 proposed regulations) to file information returns is not adopted;
claims.summary: The requirement for section 1035 issuers to file information returns is not adopted.

claims.quote: the reporting requirements under Sec.  1.6050Y-3(a) and (d) of the 2023 proposed regulations for section 1035 issuers to furnish statements are not adopted and reporting with respect to section 1035 exchanges is instead required under new Sec.  1.6050Y-3(h).
claims.summary: Reporting with respect to section 1035 exchanges is required under new Sec. 1.6050Y-3(h).

claims.quote: the old issuer will provide certain information to the new issuer, including the policyholder's investment in the contract with respect to the old interest and a statement indicating whether the old issuer would have reported a payment of reportable death benefits under Sec.  1.6050Y-4 of the final regulations had it paid death benefits attributable to the old interest on the date of the section 1035 exchange.
claims.summary: The old issuer will provide certain information to the new issuer, including the policyholder's investment in the contract with respect to the old interest and a statement indicating whether the old issuer would have reported a payment of reportable death benefits under Sec. 1.6050Y-4 of the final regulations.

claims.quote: the old issuer may use any reasonable method to provide this information to the new issuer.
claims.summary: The old issuer may use any reasonable method to provide the information to the new issuer.

claims.quote: the final regulations do not require additional reporting on the Form 1099-R, but it is anticipated that, as suggested by one of the commenters, a new distribution code for Box 7 of Form 1099-R will be added to indicate that the section 1035 exchange being reported is an exchange of an RPS contract.
claims.summary: The final regulations do not require additional reporting on the Form 1099-R.

claims.quote: Sec.  1.6050Y-3(h) of the final regulations requires the issuer of the old contract (old issuer) to notify the issuer of the new contract (new issuer) of the status of the old contract as a contract transferred, or treated as having been transferred, in an RPS and to provide the investment in the contract for the old contract.
claims.affected_party: issuer of the old contract (old issuer)
claims.summary: The issuer of the old contract must notify the issuer of the new contract of the status of the old contract as a contract transferred, or treated as having been transferred, in an RPS and provide the investment in the contract for the old contract.

claims.quote: This information is necessary to carry out the purpose of section 6050Y(c), which requires a payor of reportable death benefits to report certain information about payments of reportable death benefits.
claims.summary: The information is necessary to carry out the purpose of section 6050Y(c), which requires a payor of reportable death benefits to report certain information about payments of reportable death benefits.

claims.quote: The final regulations eliminate the reporting obligations that would have been imposed by Sec.  1.6050Y-3 of the 2023 proposed regulations on new issuers with respect to section 1035 exchanges and reduce the reporting obligations that would have been imposed by Sec.  1.6050Y-3 of the 2023 proposed regulations on old issuers with respect to section 1035 exchanges.
claims.summary: The final regulations eliminate the reporting obligations that would have been imposed by Sec. 1.6050Y-3 of the 2023 proposed regulations on new issuers with respect to section 1035 exchanges and reduce the reporting obligations that would have been imposed by Sec. 1.6050Y-3 of the 2023 proposed regulations on old issuers with respect to section 1035 exchanges.

claims.quote: The burden for the additional collection of information contained in Sec.  1.6050Y-3 of the final regulations will be reflected on Form 1099-R, Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc., when the burden is revised to reflect the additional collection of information in Sec.  1.6050Y-3.
claims.summary: The burden for the additional collection of information contained in Sec. 1.6050Y-3 of the final regulations will be reflected on Form 1099-R when the burden is revised to reflect the additional collection of information in Sec. 1.6050Y-3.

claims.quote: The burden also will be revised when a new distribution code for Box 7 of Form 1099-R is added to indicate that the section 1035 exchange being reported is an exchange of an RPS contract.
claims.summary: The burden will be revised when a new distribution code for Box 7 of Form 1099-R is added to indicate that the section 1035 exchange being reported is an exchange of an RPS contract.

claims.quote: The final regulations eliminate the burden on policyholders making section 1035 exchanges of RPS contracts imposed by Sec.  1.6050Y-2 of the 2019 final regulations.
claims.summary: The final regulations eliminate the burden on policyholders making section 1035 exchanges of RPS contracts imposed by Sec. 1.6050Y-2 of the 2019 final regulations.

claims.quote: The burden on Form 1099-LS, Reportable Life Insurance Sale, will accordingly be reduced when the burden is revised.
claims.summary: The burden on Form 1099-LS, Reportable Life Insurance Sale, will be reduced when the burden is revised.

claims.quote: The Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) requires agencies to ``prepare and make available for public comment an initial regulatory flexibility analysis,'' which will ``describe the impact of the proposed rule on small entities.''
claims.summary: Agencies must prepare and make available for public comment an initial regulatory flexibility analysis describing the impact of the proposed rule on small entities.

claims.quote: Section 605(b) of the RFA allows an agency to certify a rule, in lieu of preparing an analysis, if the proposed rulemaking is not expected to have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.
claims.summary: An agency may certify a rule instead of preparing an analysis if the proposed rulemaking is not expected to have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

claims.quote: Pursuant to the RFA, it is hereby certified that the final regulations will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities...
claims.summary: The Secretary of the Treasury certifies that the final regulations will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities.

claims.quote: Pursuant to section 7805(f) of the Code, the notice of proposed rulemaking preceding the final regulations was submitted to the Chief Counsel for the Office of Advocacy of the Small Business Administration for comment on its impact on small business, and no comments were received.
claims.summary: The notice of proposed rulemaking was submitted to the Chief Counsel for the Office of Advocacy of the Small Business Administration for comment on its impact on small business.

claims.quote: Section 202 of the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (UMRA) requires that agencies assess anticipated costs and benefits and take certain other actions before issuing a final rule that includes any Federal mandate that may result in expenditures in any one year by a State, local, or Tribal government, in the aggregate, or by the private sector, of $100 million in 1995 dollars, updated annually for inflation.
claims.summary: Agencies must assess anticipated costs and benefits and take certain other actions before issuing a final rule that includes any Federal mandate that may result in expenditures of $100 million in 1995 dollars, updated annually for inflation.

claims.quote: Executive Order 13132 (Federalism) prohibits an agency from publishing any rule that has federalism implications if the rule either imposes substantial, direct compliance costs on State and local governments, and is not required by statute, or preempts State law, unless the agency meets the consultation and funding requirements of section 6 of the Executive order.
claims.summary: An agency is prohibited from publishing any rule that has federalism implications if the rule imposes substantial, direct compliance costs on State and local governments, and is not required by statute, or preempts State law, unless the agency meets the consultation and funding requirements of section 6 of the Executive order.

claims.quote: Pursuant to the Congressional Review Act (5 U.S.C. 801 et seq.), the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs has designated this rule as not a ``major rule,'' as defined by 5 U.S.C. 804(2).
claims.affected_party: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs
claims.summary: The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs has designated this rule as not a ``major rule,'' as defined by 5 U.S.C. 804(2).

claims.quote: When an interest in a life insurance contract (old interest) is exchanged in a section 1035 exchange for an interest in a newly issued life insurance contract (new interest), except as otherwise provided by this section with respect to any portion of the new interest that is transferred or exchanged subsequent to the section 1035 exchange, the amount of the proceeds attributable to the new interest that is excludable from gross income under section 101(a) is determined under either paragraph (b)(2)(iv)(A) or paragraph (b)(2)(iv)(B) of this section.
claims.summary: The amount of proceeds excludable from gross income under section 101(a) for a new interest in a life insurance contract exchanged in a section 1035 exchange must be determined under either paragraph (b)(2)(iv)(A) or (b)(2)(iv)(B).

claims.quote: If, at the time of the exchange, the entire amount of the proceeds attributable to the old interest would have been excludable from gross income under section 101(a), the entire amount of the proceeds attributable to the new interest is excludable from gross income.
claims.summary: If the entire proceeds from the old interest would have been excludable under section 101(a), the entire proceeds from the new interest are excludable.

claims.quote: If, at the time of the exchange, less than the entire amount of the proceeds attributable to the old interest would have been excludable from gross income under section 101(a), the amount of the proceeds attributable to the new interest that is excludable from gross income is limited to the sum of the amount of the proceeds attributable to the old interest that would have been excludable at the time of the exchange and the premiums and other amounts paid with respect to the new interest by the policyholder, reduced (but not below zero) by amounts received by the policyholder under the new life insurance contract that are not received as an annuity, to the extent excludable from gross income under section 72(e). For purposes of this paragraph (b)(2)(iv)(B), the amount of the proceeds attributable to the old interest that would have been excludable at the time of the exchange is decreased by the amount of any money and the fair market value of any other property received by the policyholder in the exchange and increased by the amount of gain to the policyholder that was recognized on such exchange.
claims.summary: The excludable amount of proceeds from the new interest is limited to the sum of the excludable proceeds from the old interest, premiums paid for the new interest, and other amounts, reduced by amounts received under the new contract and increased by gain recognized on the exchange.

claims.quote: another C corporation (target C corporation) that actively conducts a trade or business within the meaning of Sec.  1.367(a)-2(d)(2) and (3);
claims.summary: The target C corporation must actively conduct a trade or business within the meaning of Sec. 1.367(a)-2(d)(2) and (3).

claims.quote: Immediately before the acquisition, the target C corporation does not engage in a trade or business of investing in interests in life insurance contracts;
claims.summary: The target C corporation must not engage in a trade or business of investing in interests in life insurance contracts immediately before the acquisition.

claims.quote: Immediately before the acquisition, no more than 5 percent of the gross value of the assets (as determined under paragraph (f)(4) of this section) of the target C corporation consists of life insurance contracts;
claims.summary: No more than 5 percent of the gross value of the assets of the target C corporation may consist of life insurance contracts immediately before the acquisition.

claims.quote: The acquisition results from a transaction that qualifies as a reorganization under section 368(a) with respect to which the target C corporation and the acquiring C corporation each is a party to the reorganization (within the meaning of section 368(b));
claims.affected_party: target C corporation and acquiring C corporation
claims.summary: The acquisition must result from a transaction that qualifies as a reorganization under section 368(a), with both the target C corporation and the acquiring C corporation being parties to the reorganization.

claims.quote: Immediately after the acquisition, the acquiring C corporation does not engage in a trade or business of investing in interests in life insurance contracts; and
claims.summary: The acquiring C corporation must not engage in a trade or business of investing in interests in life insurance contracts immediately after the acquisition.

claims.quote: Immediately after the acquisition, no more than 5 percent of the gross value of the assets (as determined under paragraph (f)(4) of this section) of the acquiring C corporation consists of life insurance contracts.
claims.summary: No more than 5 percent of the gross value of the assets of the acquiring C corporation may consist of life insurance contracts immediately after the acquisition.

claims.quote: the exception in paragraph (c)(2)(v) of this section applies, provided Corporation X satisfies the requirements of paragraphs (c)(2)(v)(A) through (C) of this section immediately before the acquisition by Corporation Y, and Corporation Y satisfies the requirements of paragraphs (c)(2)(v)(E) and (F) of this section immediately after the acquisition.
claims.summary: Corporation X must satisfy the requirements of paragraphs (c)(2)(v)(A) through (C) immediately before the acquisition, and Corporation Y must satisfy the requirements of paragraphs (c)(2)(v)(E) and (F) immediately after the acquisition.

claims.quote: the acquisition results from a transaction that qualifies as a reorganization under section 368(a) with respect to which the target C corporation and the acquiring C corporation each is a party to the reorganization (within the meaning of section 368(b));
claims.affected_party: target C corporation and acquiring C corporation
claims.summary: The acquisition must result from a transaction that qualifies as a reorganization under section 368(a), with both the target C corporation and the acquiring C corporation being parties to the reorganization.

claims.quote: the new interest is treated as an interest in a life insurance contract that previously was transferred for valuable consideration in a reportable policy sale.
claims.summary: The new interest is treated as an interest in a life insurance contract that previously was transferred for valuable consideration in a reportable policy sale.

claims.quote: the section 1035 exchange is treated as the transfer of an interest in the life insurance contract in a reportable policy sale.
claims.summary: The section 1035 exchange is treated as the transfer of an interest in the life insurance contract in a reportable policy sale.

claims.quote: Statements required to be furnished to issuers under section 6050Y(a)(2) and Sec.  1.6050Y-2(d)(2)(i) must be furnished by the later of the applicable deadline set forth in Sec.  1.6050Y-2(d)(2)(ii) or December 30, 2019.
claims.summary: Issuers must furnish statements required under section 6050Y(a)(2) and Sec. 1.6050Y-2(d)(2)(i) by the later of the applicable deadline or December 30, 2019.

claims.quote: Statements required to be furnished to reportable policy sale payment recipients under section 6050Y(a)(2) and Sec.  1.6050Y-2(d)(1)(i) must be furnished by the later of the applicable deadline set forth in Sec.  1.6050Y-2(d)(1)(ii) or February 28, 2020.
claims.summary: Reportable policy sale payment recipients must furnish statements required under section 6050Y(a)(2) and Sec. 1.6050Y-2(d)(1)(i) by the later of the applicable deadline or February 28, 2020.

claims.quote: Statements required to be furnished to sellers under section 6050Y(b)(2) and Sec.  1.6050Y-3(d)(1) must be furnished by the later of the applicable deadline set forth in Sec.  1.6050Y-3(d)(2) or February 28, 2020.
claims.summary: Sellers must furnish statements required under section 6050Y(b)(2) and Sec. 1.6050Y-3(d)(1) by the later of the applicable deadline or February 28, 2020.

claims.quote: Statements required to be furnished to reportable death benefits payment recipients under section 6050Y(c)(2) and Sec.  1.6050Y-4(c)(1) must be furnished by the later of the applicable deadline set forth in Sec.  1.6050Y-4(c)(2) or February 28, 2020.
claims.summary: Reportable death benefits payment recipients must furnish statements required under section 6050Y(c)(2) and Sec. 1.6050Y-4(c)(1) by the later of the applicable deadline or February 28, 2020.

claims.quote: Returns required to be filed under section 6050Y(a)(1) and Sec.  1.6050Y-2(a), section 6050Y(b)(1) and Sec.  1.6050Y-3(a), and section 6050Y(c)(1) and Sec.  1.6050Y-4 must be filed by the later of the applicable deadline set forth in Sec.  1.6050Y-2(c), Sec.  1.6050Y-3(c), and Sec.  1.6050Y-4(b) or February 28, 2020.
claims.summary: Returns required under section 6050Y(a)(1), (b)(1), and (c)(1) must be filed by the later of the applicable deadline or February 28, 2020.

claims.quote: (2) Provision of information. If paragraph (h)(1) of this section applies to a section 1035 exchange, the old issuer will provide to the new issuer the information necessary to ensure proper reporting of reportable death benefits under Sec. 1.6050Y-4. This information includes the policyholder's investment in the contract with respect to the old interest and a statement indicating whether the old issuer would have reported a payment of reportable death benefits under Sec. 1.6050Y-4 had it paid death benefits attributable to the old interest on the date of the section 1035 exchange.
claims.summary: The old issuer must provide the new issuer with information necessary for proper reporting of reportable death benefits under Sec. 1.6050Y-4, including the policyholder's investment and a statement about whether the old issuer would have reported a payment of reportable death benefits.

claims.quote: (3) Reasonable method. For purposes of paragraph (h)(2) of this section, the old issuer may use any reasonable method to provide the information described in paragraph (h)(2) of this section to the new issuer.
claims.summary: The old issuer may use any reasonable method to provide the information described in paragraph (h)(2) to the new issuer.

claims.quote: (3) * * * Additionally, if the reportable death benefits are paid with respect to an interest in a life insurance contract issued in a section 1035 exchange, the payor never received, and has no knowledge of any issuer having received, information indicating that the interest was issued in exchange for an interest in a life insurance contract that previously was transferred for valuable consideration in a reportable policy sale or was treated as so transferred under Sec. 1.101-1(c)(3).
claims.summary: If the reportable death benefits are paid with respect to an interest in a life insurance contract issued in a section 1035 exchange, the payor must not have received, and must not have knowledge of any issuer having received, information indicating that the interest was issued in exchange for an interest in a life insurance contract that previously was transferred for valuable consideration in a reportable policy sale or was treated as so transferred under Sec. 1.101-1(c)(3).
